sourceInformation.source: Basketball, in the over-the-top arcade style (genre inspiration; an original game with original teams, courts and characters)
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade sports: 2-on-2 basketball with a short story ladder (the Blam Tour)
sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on broadcast camera: orthographic, pitch 30 degrees, panning with the ball, with a dunk cam; optional High (three-quarter) camera
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 (modified), AI Hub session client 1.4.0, plain JavaScript, Canvas 2D, Web Audio; tests on Node 24 (node:vm headless) and Playwright 1.63 with Chromium; Python http.server for the hub harness
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native HD pixel style (PS1-era 2D at 320x240, expanded to fill the screen) pushed to a 90s arcade broadcast: HD Humanoid rigs in team jerseys, shorts and socks, hand-painted court floors, a cheated backboard, a spring net, crowds, backdrops, canvas lighting, comic banners
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's procedural Humanoid rigs, with a new pose layer over solvePose: IK hands for the dribble (synced to the ball), jump shots, 12 dunk choreographies, blocks, steals, shoves, spin moves, hanging on the rim, celebrations and taunts
sourceInformation.audio: 12 songs and 7 stings in the engine format with dynamic layers, about 50 sound effects defined in code, an Animalese/Simlish-style gibberish voice synth (formant-filtered syllables, 20+ voice profiles) for announcers, players and story characters, and a pink-noise crowd bed; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared world, 1-4 players: our own card, host-authoritative simulation, client inputs at 15/s, snapshots at 15/s with interpolation and own-player prediction, leaving players become CPU, time-up, server mode
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripts with game.advance and game.debug (tests/run.mjs: one command, prints only failures and a one-line count), including a scripted playthrough of the whole Tour; Playwright screenshots; the AI Hub harness scenarios
sourceInformation.research: None beyond reading the engine handoff docs, the sports kit and the AI Hub protocol README
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown
sourceInformation.usage: unknown (no usage figures are available inside the session)

testingFeedback: About 18 issues in the game itself (plus about 10 mistakes in the tests, fixed along the way). Examples: a shooter at the arena wall released the ball outside the wall, which halved its speed; a pass receiver wandered off instead of meeting the ball; rebounds after a rim touch were not counted; scene changes would stall while dev time was frozen; Camp handed the ball to the interns after a basket; the attract demo could miss the BLAM BOMB; dunks were 77% of baskets until rebalanced; HUD, font-glyph and layout overlaps on several screens.

3 critical: the canvas never filled the window (a 300x150 game), the custom broadcast camera was not registered so the game fell back to another view, and a frozen dev time scale would have stalled every scene change.

The headless scripted playthrough of the whole Blam Tour (tests/run.mjs tour): it drives the real menus, plays every stop with a bot holding the human seat through the real input actions, loses a stop on purpose and rematches, and reaches the ending, credits, unlocks and the Hall of Blam; along with the first CPU-vs-CPU smoke match it exposed the most bugs.
Re-taking screenshots after small layout tweaks: useful for looks, but each one cost far more time than a script and found nothing a quick check of one image would not.
engineFeedback: What I liked most: headless determinism (game.advance plus game.debug) and HD Humanoid rigs that look good with no art files.
Guessed wrong: a custom E.View must be registered in E.VIEWS for setView to find it, and the page needs the canvas sized by CSS.
The most important thing I built myself: the basketball pose layer (IK hands, a dribble synced to the ball, dunk keys) on top of solvePose.
The hardest part was depth sorting a hoop (glass, rim halves, net halves, ball) in an orthographic side view.
Engine changes: basketball shorts and socks on the Humanoid, afro, flattop and mohawk hair, a Dialog voice callback per letter, public audio buses.
One change I would make: a first-class pose and IK clip layer for rig hands, so games do not have to wrap solvePose.
promptFeedback: The complete, testable definition of done (dev mode, attract mode, hub, 10-foot UI, the report) and the freedom over genre, camera and stack; the plan made every decision concrete.

The plan was written for another model and timestamp, so its file names had to be remapped to this TASK.md; and the plan is far larger than one medium-effort session, so it was unclear how much of it was expected.
Fitting the full feature set (a story ladder, ten tutorial lessons, a five-segment attract director, a dev panel, shared-world netcode) into one session while keeping it tested.
Say how much of a large plan is in scope at a given effort level, and give the plan names that follow the TASK.md it is used with.

aiHub.name: BASKETBLAM
aiHub.tagline: No fouls. No mercy. All BLAM.
aiHub.description: Over-the-top 2-on-2 arcade basketball: turbo dunks that leave the atmosphere, legal shoves, shattered backboards and SUPERNOVA hot streaks across five wild courts, with a story Tour against a robot league, a tutorial camp and up to four players.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD move, Square/Space shoot (release at the top), R2/Shift turbo (+ shoot near the rim to dunk), Cross/E pass or steal, Circle/Q shove or spin, Triangle/F alley-oop
